Question Choices: In real-number arithmetic, evaluate 0/0. Enter undefined if the expression has no defined value.
Hints: Every number multiplied by 0 gives 0, so there is no unique quotient.
Solution: A quotient must have one defined value. The equation 0 × q = 0 holds for every real q, so it selects no unique quotient. Therefore 0/0 is undefined in real-number arithmetic. In limits, 0/0 is called an indeterminate form; that does not give this arithmetic expression a value.

Solution: Substitution makes both numerator and denominator zero. No unique quotient is defined for 0/0. Cancellation to 1 is valid only when the common factor is nonzero, so the original expression is undefined at the stated input.

Question Choices: For the expression 6/(x - 4), what value of x must be excluded from the domain?
Solution: The denominator must be nonzero. Solve x - 4 = 0: x = 4. Exclude x = 4; all other real inputs are allowed.
